title: Telemetry noise fingerprinting and attenuation pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current anomaly alerts surface a high rate of low-value noise (instrumentation spikes, retry storms, transient routing blips) that increases pager fatigue and hides real incidents affecting latency, cost, and usage. Existing detectors trigger on raw thresholds or rolling-z scores which are sensitive to structured noise patterns (short bursts, periodic outliers, tag-churn).

Goal: Build a telemetry pre-processing pipeline that fingerprints recurring noise patterns and attenuates their influence on downstream anomaly detection and alerting. The pipeline should: 1) identify short-lived burst patterns and mark them as low-confidence events, 2) compute per-metric noise fingerprints (e.g., periodicity, burst-length distribution, upstream-release-correlated spikes), 3) expose an adjustable attenuation factor per fingerprint to downstream detectors, and 4) produce explainable annotations for alerts in the Console (why an event was suppressed or downranked).

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement new detector algorithms (e.g., ML-based RCA); it augments the signal pre-processing stage. It also does not replace existing incident escalation policies or on-call routing logic.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A new streaming preprocessing microservice (telemetry-noise-agent) runs in the observability cluster and subscribes to the intra-console telemetry Kafka topic.
2) The service classifies >90% of known historical retry storms and deployment-related bursts into fingerprint classes with >85% precision on a labeled validation set.
3) Downstream anomaly detector (existing pipeline) receives an `attenuation_factor` header and reduces alert score contribution by that factor.
4) Console UI shows a human-readable annotation for attenuated alerts with root fingerprint and confidence.
5) Integration tests and load tests show <5% added end-to-end alert latency at p95 under normal traffic and acceptable backpressure behavior under spike loads.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: lightweight streaming service written in Go, running as k8s Deployment in observability namespace. It will consume from `telemetry.events.v1` Kafka topic (AVRO), run a small fingerprinting engine (rule-based + micro-ML features), and emit enriched events to `telemetry.events.enriched.v1`. Attenuation factor will be a float in [0,1] attached as message header and event field.

Fingerprinting heuristics: burst-length histogram, inter-arrival time distribution, metric-tag correlation, rolling-FFT for periodic signals, and simple signature hashing for repeated sequences. Keep models tiny (linear/logistic) to avoid GPU/Heavy deps. Configuration via ConfigMap and feature flags for gradual rollout.

Data retention: store fingerprint summaries in Redis (TTL 7d) for fast lookup; persistent snapshot to ClickHouse for offline evaluation and auditability.

Trade-offs: rule-first approach gets us quick coverage and explainability; may miss subtle anomalies that only ML finds. We accept this as iteration 1 to reduce operational noise quickly.
risks:
1) Misclassification could suppress legitimate incidents — mitigated by conservative default attenuation (0.6) and monitor for false-suppression.
2) Extra processing could add latency to alerting — mitigated by async enrichment path and p95 budget.
3) New state store (Redis) needs HA and cost consideration for scale — proposal to reuse existing obs-redis cluster.
4) Edge cases with multi-tenant metrics where fingerprinting must be tenant-aware to avoid cross-tenant contamination.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting logic and attenuation calculation. Integration test harness that replays historical telemetry (last 90 days) through the service and compares alerting outputs against baseline. Load test: replay synthetic peak-traces at 2x expected peak ingest to validate p95 latency and Kafka consumer lag behavior. Post-deploy: a 2-week canary with attenuation factor ramped from 0.8 -> 0.6 -> 0.4 and daily validation against labeled incidents.
qa_checklist:
- [ ] Unit test coverage >80% for core heuristics
- [ ] End-to-end replay test passes and documents false-suppression rate
- [ ] Feature flag gating ready for rollout
- [ ] Dashboard to monitor fingerprint class counts and attenuation distribution
- [ ] Runbook updated with how to rollback attenuation and how to expunge a fingerprint
deployment_plan:
1) Deploy telemetry-noise-agent to staging with feature flag disabled for enrichment.
2) Run replay validation and load tests.
3) Enable enrichment for 5% of traffic via sampler config for 48 hours. Monitor key metrics and false-suppression.
4) Gradually increase sample to 25%, 75%, then 100% while tuning heuristics.
5) Post-mortem and tweak thresholds after 2-week observation window.
notes:
We plan to collaborate with SRE (Helena Chen) for Redis sizing and Kafka partitioning, and with Product (Rafael Gomez) for Console annotation copy. Reach out to Research (Priya Nair) if we want to prototype an ML-based fingerprinter after iteration 1.

comments: 2025-11-13 — Initial spike analysis completed. Identified 3 recurring fingerprint candidates: deployment-rollout-burst, client-retry-loop, and noisy-ingestion-kafka-lag. (Marco)

2025-11-15 — Design review with PM and SRE. Decided to use Redis for short-term fingerprint state and ClickHouse for snapshots. SRE flagged need to limit memory per-key. Action: add cardinality cap and LRU policy. (Aisha)
2025-11-17 — Proto implementation pushed to branch telemetry-noise-agent. Added simple burst-length histogram and attenuation header emission. PR #1872 opened for early feedback. (Marco)

2025-11-19 — QA: Replay harness shows 72% reduction in low-value alerts for last 30 days in staging when attenuation_factor <= 0.6; two legitimate incidents were lightly attenuated — tracking as follow-up tuning task. (QA Team)
2025-11-20 — Action items: add tenant-scoped fingerprints, add explanation text for Console UI, and schedule a canary rollout for 2025-11-25. (Aisha)
